description: Trace Cromwell’s Ely years, a medieval monastic gate and the city’s riverside malting trade before returning beneath the cathedral towers.
author: Day Tripping Quiz

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Before crowns fell and armies marched, the future Lord Protector called this timber-framed house home.
stops.Hint_1: Search near the cathedral for a heavily timbered house linked to Oliver Cromwell.
stops.Hint_2: Find the building carrying Cromwell’s name and an information plaque.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Oliver Cromwell and his family lived in Ely for roughly a decade from 1636. The surviving timber-framed house is now a visitor attraction and also contains Ely’s tourist information centre.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Look at the exterior timber pattern and describe one shape made by the beams.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Monks once passed through this mighty gate; scholars now walk where the monastery stood.
stops.Hint_1: Walk south through the cathedral precinct and look for a large medieval gateway.
stops.Hint_2: Find the tall brick-and-stone arch known as The Porta.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The Porta was completed in 1397 as the main gatehouse to Ely’s medieval monastery precinct. It survives as part of King’s Ely school.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Notice the mix of brick and stone and record which material frames the main arch.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Barley once climbed my floors beside the river before returning as malt for a brewer.
stops.Hint_1: Descend towards Waterside and the River Great Ouse.
stops.Hint_2: Find the large brick Maltings building dated 1868.
stops.Unlock_Fact: The Maltings was built in 1868 for brewer Ebenezer William Harlock. Barley was processed here beside the Great Ouse; the landmark now serves as an events and community venue.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: Find the dated gable and note the initials displayed with 1868.

stops.Cryptic_Clue: Return to the great west tower for a tavern that borrows its neighbour’s churchly title.
stops.Hint_1: Climb back towards the cathedral’s west front.
stops.Hint_2: Find the traditional pub at 1 Minster Place, opposite the cathedral.
stops.Unlock_Fact: Route complete! The Minster Tavern is a traditional old pub opposite Ely Cathedral’s west tower and is described locally as the city’s oldest pub. Stop for food or a drink if it is open.
stops.Explorer_Prompt: From outside, find one detail in the pub frontage that echoes its historic setting.

short_description: Follow Cromwell, monastic Ely and the malt trade from cathedral hill to Waterside.

before_you_go.terrain: Town pavements, historic precinct paths and a paved riverside section around The Maltings.
before_you_go.hills: Expect a noticeable descent from the cathedral area to Waterside and a climb back for the finish.
before_you_go.steps: The intended outdoor route avoids required steps, although the sloping alternatives are longer.
before_you_go.accessibility: The checkpoints are viewable outdoors; gradients, older paving and temporary cathedral-precinct works may affect step-free travel.
before_you_go.toilets: Check current cathedral, council and Waterside visitor-facility information before setting out.
before_you_go.footwear: Wear comfortable shoes with grip for the climb and potentially damp riverside paving.
before_you_go.dogs: The outdoor route suits dogs kept under control; check the Minster Tavern’s current policy separately.
before_you_go.pushchairs: Possible throughout on the intended route, but the Waterside climb may be tiring with a pushchair.

recommended_age: Recommended 8+; under-18s with an adult; check final venue policy
transport_note: A there-and-back city walk between the cathedral precinct and Waterside, including a noticeable hill.
